basis: Corpus callosum agenesis establishes CNS malformation; unspecified facial clefting does not establish oral involvement.

decisions.gastrointestinal: none: facial cleft anatomy is unspecified; cleft palate or another oral structural defect is not established.

basis: Medication-induced dysfunction of brainstem respiratory control defines the disorder; intrinsic lung or airway disease is not established. Cardiovascular consequences are later risks.

decisions.pulmonary: none: apnea results from impaired central respiratory signaling; the definition establishes no disease of lung tissue or airways.

basis: Inherited amino-acid transport disorders impair proximal renal tubular reabsorption; renal location and inborn metabolic mechanism define the group.

decisions.metabolic_endocrine: primary: inherited defects of amino-acid transport qualify as inborn metabolic disorders, even without systemic metabolic complications.

basis: Pituitary GH excess and pathological skeletal overgrowth define gigantism; myocardial hypertrophy/cardiomyopathy is annotated in 80-99%.

decisions.musculoskeletal: primary: excessive skeletal growth before epiphyseal closure defines gigantism; accelerated skeletal maturation and acral/jaw overgrowth support this axis.

basis: Malignant mesenchymal soft-tissue neoplasm in the solitary fibrous tumor spectrum; no specific visceral origin is supplied.

decisions.cardiovascular: none: prominent perivascular architecture does not establish a vascular-organ malignancy or vascular dysfunction.
decisions.musculoskeletal: primary: this is a mesenchymal soft-tissue tumor in the solitary fibrous tumor spectrum, without a specified visceral site.

basis: Postsynaptic neuromuscular-junction disease; ocular and generalized weakness reflect transmission failure. Scoliosis 1/2 and hyperlordosis 2/5 are secondary skeletal manifestations.

decisions.ocular: none: ptosis 8/8 and ophthalmoplegia 6/6 reflect neuromuscular transmission failure, without direct disease of ocular structures.
decisions.musculoskeletal: none: weakness and amyotrophy reflect neuromuscular dysfunction; scoliosis 1/2 and hyperlordosis 2/5 are secondary deformities, not direct skeletal disease.

basis: Peripheral neuropathy is explicitly defined by an endocrine etiology; neurologic injury and the endocrine mechanism are integral to this concept.

decisions.metabolic_endocrine: primary: endocrine causation is a defining component of this etiologically specified neuropathy, supporting the endocrine mechanism axis.

basis: The tumor originates in peritoneal fibroblastic tissue, outside the explicitly covered organs; direct involvement of bowel or another covered organ is not established.

decisions.gastrointestinal: none: peritoneal origin alone does not establish disease of the listed gastrointestinal organs; bowel involvement is not documented.

basis: GM2 storage causes progressive central and peripheral neurodegeneration; muscle atrophy/weakness at 30-79% is neurogenic, without established direct muscle disease.

decisions.musculoskeletal: none: frequent muscle atrophy and weakness (30-79%) reflect motor-neuron/peripheral nerve degeneration; direct myopathy is not established.

basis: Liver failure/cholestasis 2/2; skeletal defects 2/2; renal agenesis/hydronephrosis 1/2. Cardiac defects 1/2 omitted by cap; low anticoagulants may reflect liver failure.

decisions.haematologic: none: reduced protein C and antithrombin activity in 2/2 may reflect hepatic failure; independent direct coagulation disease is not established.
decisions.hepatic: primary: severe hepatic failure and cholestasis in 2/2 establish the dominant organ phenotype of this glycosylation disorder.
decisions.renal: involved: renal agenesis and hydronephrosis each occur in 1/2 reported patients, meeting the frequency threshold for structural renal involvement.
